first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and simplifying onboarding directly addresses the shared funnel constraint with prior evidence of faster time-to-value and early adoption. Promotional pricing is highly consequential given the competitor move, but its claimed revenue lift needs verification against long-term qualified-revenue and value-dilution risk before committing the sole experiment slot. Verify the directly relevant onboarding result and the pricing alternative with the largest downstream-value uncertainty.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified prior result directly addresses the current 4% onboarding-completion decline and adjacent 6% activation decline, with completion up 13%, time-to-value reduced by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention up 3%. This is better aligned with sustainable qualified revenue than promotional pricing, whose verified discounted cohort failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Measure qualified revenue, meaningful activation, and retention by segment; do not assume this alone resolves competitor-driven price-sensitive SMB losses.
